topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s importance and warns about the difficulty of complement nomenclature before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Foundations of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual and molecular framework for understanding complement as a cascade centred on C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition produces enough surface-bound C3b to cross the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement drives the elimination of pathogens.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how pathogens evade complement and how one such evasion mechanism is exploited medically and experimentally.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the complement lecture and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
